🔔 Bitcoin price nears Fidelity’s power law support: Accumulation zone or missing catalyst? 

📌 On his power law model, a logarithmic chart that bounds Bitcoin’s entire price history between an upper resistance curve, a middle trendline, and a lower support curve, the floor currently sits near 58,000 dollars. That lower line has caught every major Bitcoin bottom since 2015. Timmer’s label for the zone the market has now entered is unambiguous: accumulation. His caveat is just as unambiguous: he sees no catalyst for a reversal, and he is not calling a bottom.

⚠️ That combination, a historically reliable floor approaching and a strategist refusing to ring the bell, is the most honest summary of the Bitcoin market in July 2026. The asset is coming off its worst quarter since the 2022 bear market, spot ETFs just recorded their largest quarterly outflow since launch, the speculative premium that carried the price past 120,000 dollars last year has evaporated, and the fast money has visibly rotated elsewhere, first into gold, then into semiconductor stocks. And yet the two quantitative measures Timmer trusts most, the deviation from the power law trendline and the Bitcoin-to-gold ratio, have both sunk to depths recorded at exactly two prior moments: the 2018 low and the 2022 low. Both of those moments were generational buying opportunities. Both also felt like the end of the world at the time.

🔖 This feature takes the model seriously in both directions: what the power law actually says, why its track record earns attention, and why the missing-catalyst objection is not a hedge but the core of the analysis.

📌 Tehran, IRNA – President Masoud Pezeshkian, emphasizing the need for the systematic legal pursuit of US-Israeli crimes against the Iranian nation, says that steps must be taken to strengthen the country's legal deterrence power and influence in international arenas.

Pezeshkian made the remarks on Saturday while chairing a specialized meeting attended by Minister of Justice Ayatollah Mohaghegh Damad and a group of prominent experts. ​

The president added that Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Judiciary Chief Gholamhossein Mohseni-Ejei deserve appreciation, as they have always backed the administration with full commitment—despite occasionally facing what he described as unfair criticism.

🖥 France vs England: World Cup third-place playoff team news and lineups

📌 France vs England face off in the 2026 World Cup third-place playoff. Get the ultimate match preview, predicted lineup, injury news, and how to watch here.

Still reeling from semi-final heartbreak, France and England face off in a World Cup match neither would have chosen—a third-place playoff offering little more than a figurative bronze medal. Firm favorites to add a third World Cup title, in-form France were outclassed by stalwarts Spain, while England’s agonizing six-decade wait for a major trophy continued following a late, cruel defeat to defending champions Argentina. A day before the world tunes in to watch the final, France vs England serves as the ultimate match preview of resilience. With Didier Deschamps bowing out after 14 years and Kylian Mbappe chasing back-to-back Golden Boots, this clash at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens holds hidden stakes for both proud footballing nations.
​
With the title no longer in reach, both sides are expected to rotate heavily and offer game time to players who otherwise had fewer minutes. However, key injury news dictates several forced changes for both managers.
​
Manager Didier Deschamps will be without instrumental center-back William Saliba, who withdrew against Spain due to a back injury. Goalkeeper Brice Samba is also dealing with a calf issue, meaning Mike Maignan should keep his place. With changes expected, Maxence Lacroix is primed to step in at the back, while Desire Doue and Rayan Cherki could inject youth into the attack. Kylian Mbappe is guaranteed to start as he hunts down the Golden Boot.
​
Thomas Tuchel’s squad is battling intense fatigue. Jordan Henderson is definitively ruled out after breaking his wrist, and Declan Rice will be rested after struggling with his fitness all tournament. Reece James remains doubtful with a muscle issue, but could step into midfield if passed fit. Bukayo Saka is not completely fit, opening the door for Noni Madueke to start on the right wing.
​
Both managers have been remarkably candid about the dreaded nature of this fixture.
​
This is the 33rd meeting between France and England, with the Three Lions historically holding the edge, though recent history favors the French.
​
This is their 4th World Cup meeting. England won the first two (2-0 in 1966, 3-1 in 1982), but France won 2-1 in the 2022 quarter-final. Overall, England have won just one of their last nine matches against France (1W, 2D, 6L).
​
France’s double pivot of Koné and Zaïre-Emery feeds Olise — the tournament’s top assister with 5 — and Mbappé, whose 11 goal involvements make him the most dangerous player on the pitch. England’s reshuffled 4-3-3 must win second balls and press early, because dropping deep against this France attack is a losing formula.
​
The numbers tell the real story: France concede 0.57 goals per game versus England’s 1.14, and that defensive gap widens with Saliba absent and England’s backline rotated. Tuchel’s side has pace up front through Madueke, Kane, and Rashford to threaten transitions, but they must do it against a side that has kept four clean sheets this tournament. France carry the higher ceiling — Deschamps’ farewell adds fuel — but England’s 60-year milestone target makes this anything but a formality.
